newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel suspends re-election session.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel suspends re-election session.

text.p: A Brazil Senate committee suspended until Wednesday a session which was due to study and possibly vote on a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election.
The panel also defeated a motion proposed by a left-wing opposition party that all voting on re-election be suspended pending investigations into a new corruption scandal involving the legislation.
Nineteen members of the Constitution and Justice Committee voted against the motion and four voted in favor.

Earlier Tuesday, newspaper Folha de Sao Paulo published a transcript of a recorded telephone conversation which it alleged showed five members of the Chamber of Deputies received payment in return for their votes for the re-election bill.
The newspaper alleged the payments were made by the governors of Acre and Amazonas state, Orleir Campeli and Amazonino Mendes.
The report stung Brazilian Bradies with the government's C bonds 5/8 lower at 76-3/8 in London.
Government-allied senators sought to play down the scandal and said there was no sign of any involvement by the government.

"In no way was the government or the president involved in this. There is no indication that is the case," said Senator Sergio Machado, upper house leader of Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Party.

The re-election bill had been due to be studied and possibly voted by the committee where it has already been approved once. It was returned to the committee after four amendments were proposed on the Senate floor.
One of those amendments would force state governors seeking re-election to stand down from office for six months prior to election day.
The proposal is reported to have the backing of about half of the Senate's 81 members who intend to stand as state governors next year and do not relish taking on sitting candidates.
